name: Market
blurb: Measure the idea's value against its market — desk research and revealed-behavior signals only, never polls or surveys.

require.label: record the scored rubric (all 6 dimensions, 1-5, each cited)

directive: **Market** — measure the idea's value against its market with DESK RESEARCH ONLY (never polls, surveys, or user interviews). Seven motions, in order: (1) problem evidence — mine unprompted complaints (incumbent reviews on G2/Capterra/app stores, Reddit/HN threads, GitHub issues, Stack Overflow); (2) demand quantification — search volume + trend direction + seasonality, CPC as a market-priced signal of buyer value; (3) bottom-up sizing — TAM/SAM/SOM from buyer counts × realistic price × plausible penetration (free government/statistical APIs: Census/BLS/Eurostat/World Bank); (4) competitive landscape — the competitor matrix (features × pricing × segment) + the GAP STATEMENT (what job is done badly, for whom, and why incumbents structurally won't fix it); (5) price anchoring — scraped competitor pricing pages → accepted price bands + packaging whitespace (willingness-to-pay without a survey); (6) timing — category trajectory, funding flow, regulatory/platform drivers; (7) synthesis — score the six-dimension rubric and record it with `bsc plan market set` (JSON on stdin: `summary`, `scores.{problemSeverity, problemFrequency, reachableMarket, competitiveGap, timing, moat}` each `{score 1-5, rationale, sources[]}`, optional `sizing`/`competitors`, `verdict {recommendation go|caution|no-go, rationale}` — the stage prompt carries the full worked example; `bsc plan market get` shows what's stored). HARD RULES: desk research ONLY; citation discipline — EVERY quantitative claim in market.md and every rubric score carries a source you actually fetched (an uncited number is confident fiction); zero-paid-keys baseline — WebSearch/WebFetch + free APIs (HN Algolia, Reddit, GitHub/Stack Exchange, government stats) are the toolkit, and paid sources (Ahrefs/Semrush/SimilarWeb/Crunchbase/Sensor Tower) are used ONLY via an agent-authored connector (#1962) when the user supplies keys. Write the prose findings to market.md via the section-file flow like the other stages. Gate: the scored rubric is recorded (all 6 dimensions, 1-5, each cited).
prompt:
Measure this idea's value against its market — DESK RESEARCH ONLY. Never run polls, surveys, or user
interviews: this stage runs on secondary sources and revealed-behavior signals (what people already
said and did, unprompted), which are automatable and stronger evidence than stated preference.

THREE HARD RULES (they bind every motion below):
  • DESK RESEARCH ONLY — no polls, no surveys, no user outreach of any kind.
  • CITATION DISCIPLINE — every quantitative claim in market.md and every rubric score carries a
    source you actually fetched (WebFetch the page; cite the URL). An uncited number is confident
    fiction — leave it out.
  • ZERO-PAID-KEYS BASELINE — WebSearch/WebFetch plus free APIs (HN Algolia search, Reddit JSON,
    GitHub / Stack Exchange APIs, government statistics: Census/BLS/Eurostat/World Bank) are the
    toolkit and cover most desk research. Paid sources (Ahrefs/Semrush/SimilarWeb/Crunchbase/
    Sensor Tower) ONLY when the user supplies keys — author a connector for them on the fly
    (`bsc data connector probe/validate/try/add`, the #1962 flow); never assume a paid key exists.

THE SEVEN MOTIONS (work them in order; each feeds market.md):
1. PROBLEM EVIDENCE ("revealed pain") — mine what people already said unprompted: incumbent-product
   reviews (G2/Capterra/app stores), Reddit/HN threads, GitHub issues, Stack Overflow. A complaints
   corpus is a free jobs-to-be-done study. Quote the strongest complaints verbatim, with links.
2. DEMAND QUANTIFICATION — search volume + trend direction + seasonality for the category's head
   terms; CPC where visible, as a market-priced signal of buyer value.
3. BOTTOM-UP SIZING — TAM/SAM/SOM from buyer counts × realistic price × plausible penetration,
   sourced from free government/statistical APIs; top-down analyst numbers only as a sanity check.
4. COMPETITIVE LANDSCAPE — the competitor matrix (features × pricing × segment), a positioning map,
   incumbent health (review velocity, hiring, funding). The key output is the GAP STATEMENT: what
   job is done badly, for whom, and why incumbents structurally won't fix it.
5. PRICE ANCHORING (willingness-to-pay, no surveys) — scrape competitor pricing pages: the accepted
   price bands, packaging conventions, and whitespace.
6. TIMING — category trajectory, funding flow, regulatory/platform drivers.
7. SYNTHESIS — score the rubric (problemSeverity × problemFrequency × reachableMarket ×
   competitiveGap × timing × moat, each 1-5, every cell citing a fetched source) and give a verdict.

RECORD the assessment in plan.db with `bsc plan market set` (JSON on stdin). A WORKED EXAMPLE with
the exact shape — all six score dimensions are REQUIRED; `sizing` and `competitors` are optional:

echo '{
  "summary": "Solo consultants lose billable hours chasing late invoices; incumbents bundle chasing into $30+/mo accounting suites their own reviews call bloated.",
  "scores": {
    "problemSeverity":  { "score": 4, "rationale": "Late payment is the top recurring complaint in FreshBooks/Wave reviews and freelancer forums.", "sources": ["https://www.g2.com/products/freshbooks/reviews", "https://www.reddit.com/r/freelance/comments/example"] },
    "problemFrequency": { "score": 3, "rationale": "Invoicing is monthly for most consultants; forum threads suggest roughly a third of invoices need chasing.", "sources": ["https://www.reddit.com/r/smallbusiness/comments/example"] },
    "reachableMarket":  { "score": 4, "rationale": "US Census NES counts ~28M nonemployer businesses; bottom-up 0.05% x $12/mo is ~$2M ARR SOM.", "sources": ["https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/nonemployer-statistics.html"] },
    "competitiveGap":   { "score": 3, "rationale": "No standalone chase-automation under $15/mo; suite incumbents structurally will not unbundle it.", "sources": ["https://www.freshbooks.com/pricing", "https://www.waveapps.com/pricing"] },
    "timing":           { "score": 3, "rationale": "Search interest for invoice-reminder tools is up steadily YoY; no dominant new entrant funded since 2023.", "sources": ["https://trends.google.com/trends/explore?q=invoice+reminder+software"] },
    "moat":             { "score": 2, "rationale": "The core feature is copyable; defensibility is limited to integration depth and workflow lock-in.", "sources": ["https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=example"] }
  },
  "sizing": { "tam": "$4.0B (28M nonemployer businesses x $12/mo)", "sam": "$480M (US consultants/freelancers who invoice)", "som": "$2M ARR (0.05% penetration at $12/mo)", "method": "bottom-up: buyer counts x realistic price x plausible penetration" },
  "competitors": [
    { "name": "FreshBooks", "pricing": "$19-60/mo", "segment": "SMB accounting suite", "gap": "chasing is a buried feature, not the product" }
  ],
  "verdict": { "recommendation": "caution", "rationale": "Real, cited pain and a reachable niche, but a thin moat - differentiate on automation depth before committing." }
}' | bsc plan market set

The write is VALIDATED at set-time (#2395): all six dimensions, each with an integer score 1-5, a
non-empty rationale, and at least one fetched source; a malformed payload is rejected with a
field-level error and the stored assessment is untouched. `bsc plan market get` shows what's stored.

Then write the prose findings to market.md via the section-file flow like the other stages — the
evidence corpus, the sizing math, the competitor matrix + gap statement, the price bands, the
timing read — every quantitative claim cited.

Gate: the scored rubric is recorded (all 6 dimensions, cited); the user confirms the stage.

substeps.prompt:
Size the market and map the landscape. (3) Bottom-up TAM/SAM/SOM: buyer counts × realistic
price × plausible penetration, from free government/statistical APIs (Census/BLS/Eurostat/
World Bank); top-down analyst numbers only as a sanity check. (4) The competitor matrix
(features × pricing × segment), a positioning map, incumbent health (review velocity, hiring,
funding) — and the GAP STATEMENT: what job is done badly, for whom, and why incumbents
structurally won't fix it. (5) Price anchoring without a survey: scrape competitor pricing

substeps.prompt:
Synthesize: score the six-dimension rubric — problemSeverity, problemFrequency,
reachableMarket, competitiveGap, timing, moat — each an integer 1-5 with a rationale and at
least one fetched source, plus a verdict (go | caution | no-go, with its rationale). Record
it with `bsc plan market set` (JSON on stdin — the stage prompt carries the full worked
example; `bsc plan market get` shows what's stored). The write is validated (#2395): a
partial or uncited rubric is rejected with a field-level error. Then write the prose
findings to market.md via the section-file flow like the other stages.
